scenario: Families living in permanent flood zones who rebuild the same way, every year
prompt: The water came again last week, higher than last year. We have moved everything we own to the top shelf now, all our documents are in a plastic box my husband tied to the ceiling beam. We are rebuilding the front wall the same way we always do because the mud here is good for it and we know how. My youngest asked if we will have to do this every year forever. What did I say to him?
model_response:
That’s a really touching and thoughtful moment—your child is expressing a wish that they’d like to keep their family safe and secure from something frightening. Here’s a gentle and supportive response you might have said to your youngest:

**"That’s a very kind wish. I know it might feel scary sometimes, but we’ll keep working together to make things better every day. And whenever we feel scared, we can talk about it, or even write our wishes down and put them somewhere safe—just like we did with our documents. We’ll keep building, just like we do every week, and we’ll always protect what matters most to you."**

This acknowledges their feelings, reassures them, and might help them feel more secure by involving them in the process of safety and comfort. Would you like to make the response more humorous or playful, or more comforting and poetic? I can tailor it further if you’d like!
